readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckActualSpatialCoefficients.actual_spatial_coefficients
readback.mathematical_statement: E is the fixed real three-dimensional Euclidean space ClosedSmoothModel 3, Bilin is E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R, Jet1 is E ->L[R] Bilin, Jet2 is E ->L[R] Jet1, and Variables is (Bilin times Jet1) times Jet2. For arbitrary universe u, let M : Type u have a topology, be Hausdorff, carry an E charted-space structure, and be C-infinity for closedSmoothModelWithCorners 3. Let g0 and bg be any actual ClosedSmoothRiemannianMetric 3 M, and anchor any point of M. No CompactSpace, connectedness, curvature, flow, atlas, coefficient, derivative, or operator package is supplied as an additional premise. The literal explicitly defines G0(z) as the global-root CovariantDerivative.chartMetric with I fixed to closedSmoothModelWithCorners 3, using g0.inner and this anchor. Thus G0 is the actual bilinear metric pullback through the tangent map of the inverse preferred chart, using the same boundaryless model and chart structure as the metric data; no alternative implicit model with corners is selected. It explicitly defines B(z) as the actual GeodesicTransport.chartChristoffelField bg anchor, a continuous-bilinear E-valued background connection field. Let C be extChartAt(closedSmoothModelWithCorners 3,anchor) and chi be the fixed GeodesicTransport cutoff based at anchor. U is the specific set C.target intersect {z in E | chi equals one on a full ambient E neighborhood of z}. The predicate uses Filter.Eventually at nhds z, not a within-set filter or merely pointwise chi(z)=1. U is defined from the actual chart and cutoff; it is not an arbitrary existentially chosen open set. The theorem concludes that U is open and that G0(z) is CLM.IsInvertible for every z in U, meaning the bilinear form as E -> E dual is the forward map of a continuous linear equivalence. This invertibility is a conclusion from the actual metric/chart geometry, not a new input assumption. It also concludes that for every i,j : Fin 3, the real-valued field z |-> inverseEntries(G0(z))_(i,j) is C-infinity on U. inverseEntries is the actual full Matrix.inv of the coordinate matrix G0(z)(e_i)(e_j), with e_i=basis3 i, not entrywise reciprocal or pointwise inverse of a function. The public entry regularity uses the original real and Bilin structures and exports no Matrix norm choice. Next the theorem concludes C-infinity on U of the actual operator-valued zeroOrder field z |-> zeroOrder(B(z),D B(z),G0(z),D G0(z),D2 G0(z)) and of the actual operator-valued firstOrder field z |-> firstOrder(B(z),D B(z),G0(z),D G0(z)). Here D and D2 are ordinary fderiv R and fderiv R (fderiv R), evaluated at z. Thus background derivative and the first/second metric jets are the actual spatial derivatives of these defined fields, not independently supplied data. zeroOrder is a CLM Bilin -> Bilin, and firstOrder a CLM Jet1 -> Bilin. Their smoothness is in the whole existing CLM operator-norm topology, not merely scalar smoothness after choosing variation directions or tensor slots. C-infinity is ContDiffOn R at the ENat top injected into WithTop ENat, rather than the outer top regularity value. The pinned zeroOrder(B,DB,G,J,H) is the sum over every i,j : Fin 3 of inverseEntryDerivative G i j smulRight H(e_i)(e_j), plus lowerDifferential B DB G J composed with the inl map hG |-> (hG,0). Applied to a variation hG it retains the full inverse variation -sum_(k,l) a(G)_(i,k) * hG(e_k)(e_l) * a(G)_(l,j), contracted against H(e_i)(e_j), as well as the actual metric partial derivative of lowerTerm. The pinned firstOrder is lowerDifferential B DB G J composed with inr, taking hJ |-> (0,hJ). lowerDifferential is the actual existing fderiv in only G,J of lowerTerm B DB G J, with the background value/derivative fixed during the metric direction. These definitions exclude background variation from the PDE variation while permitting the background fields to vary spatially in the coefficient maps. Finally, for every z in U and every arbitrary h=((hG,hJ),hH) in Variables, the theorem concludes the equality of whole Bilin outputs: differential(B(z),D B(z),G0(z),D G0(z),D2 G0(z))(h) = principal(G0(z),hH) + zeroOrder(B(z),D B(z),G0(z),D G0(z),D2 G0(z))(hG) + firstOrder(B(z),D B(z),G0(z),D G0(z))(hJ). principal(G,hH) is the double sum over i,j of inverseEntries G i j smul hH(e_i)(e_j). The v3 local Gz,Jz,Hz,Bz,DBz bindings in this final clause are exactly the displayed evaluations G0(z),D G0(z),D2 G0(z),B(z),D B(z); they cache these values and do not add assumptions, replace derivatives, or change the decomposition. The zero-order term therefore retains Da(G0(z))[hG] applied to the actual D2 G0(z), rather than dropping this principal-coefficient variation. The literal uses canonical CLM groups and real normed spaces for Jet1,Jet2,background spaces and zero-/first-order output operator spaces, plus canonical Prod group/space and additive-monoid caches. Their explicit real scalars and identity ring homomorphisms preserve original CLM operator norms, standard product operations and real scalar actions; no alternative norm or supplied instance hypothesis is introduced. The regularity and decomposition are asserted only on the actual U. The statement does not assert smoothness outside that chart/cutoff-one zone, compact-buffer coefficient bounds, a time or Hoelder lifespan, differentiated tensor covariance, a bounded global L, a signed global L/P/R identity or contraction, or physical Ricci flow, Hamilton convergence, smoothability, or the final Poincare theorem. It decomposes the existing actual finite-jet differential and does not reassert its separate HasFDerivAt certificate as a new clause.
